evidence.quote: Initial evaluation at a local hospital diagnosed acute sinusitis.

preoperative differential diagnoses included “1. Left acute sinusitis (invasive fungal sinusitis to be ruled out), 2. Left nasal lymphoma to be ruled out.”

events.description: Endoscopic sinus surgery of the left maxillary and ethmoid sinuses

evidence.quote: Endoscopic sinus surgery for the left maxillary and ethmoid sinuses was performed on 15 January 2025.
Intraoperative findings included diffuse mucosal swelling of the left nasal cavity and septum, swollen maxillary sinus mucosa with cheesy purulent plaques, and hyperplastic, sclerotic ethmoid bone.
Frozen section histopathology revealed extensive lymphoid proliferation, suggestive of lymphoma pending definitive histology and immunohistochemistry (IHC).

events.description: Postoperative intravenous cefoperazone/sulbactam and methylprednisolone started

evidence.quote: Postoperatively, intravenous cefoperazone/sulbactam (2 g q8h) and methylprednisolone (40 mg daily, tapered to 8 mg daily over 3 days) were initiated.
Headache showed transient improvement.
Blood analysis (18 January 2025) showed marked elevation of C-reactive protein (100.3 mg/L).
Definitive histopathology (23 January) confirmed chronic mucosal inflammation with lymphoid hyperplasia.
Cranial MRI and lumbar puncture (24 January) were unremarkable, including normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure, routine analysis, and biochemistry.

events.description: Antibiotic de-escalation to imipenem/cilastatin after Infectious Disease consultation

Her underlying Bartter syndrome triggered severe postoperative hypokalemia (2.55 mmol/L ↓) and hypomagnesemia (0.39 mmol/L ↓) on 25 January.

events.description: Immunosuppressants withheld; intravenous magnesium sulfate and oral potassium chloride started

evidence.quote: Immunosuppressants were temporarily withheld, with initiation of aggressive intravenous magnesium sulfate and high-dose oral potassium chloride supplementation.
As infectious and neoplastic etiologies failed to fully explain the clinical course, rheumatology/immunology consultation was sought.
Immunological workup on 25 January revealed elevated complement C3 (2.00 g/L ↑) and C1q (388 mg/L ↑), and a positive anti-PR3 IgG antibody (36.1 (++) AU/mL ↑).
High-resolution chest CT on 27 January 2025, identified a cavitary nodule in the posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe, suggestive of a granulomatous lesion (Figure 2C).
Concurrent urinalysis showed no hematuria, proteinuria, or cellular casts.
GPA was ultimately diagnosed based on PR3-ANCA seropositivity and chest CT findings of cavitary pulmonary nodules.

summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with Bartter syndrome diagnosed 8 years earlier and managed with calcium carbonate and sodium–potassium–magnesium supplementation presented with a 1-month history of left-sided nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, epistaxis and headache. Symptoms began in late November 2024, and a local hospital diagnosed acute sinusitis. Saline irrigation, mometasone, oral cefuroxime and later intravenous ceftriaxone gave no relief.

Nasal endoscopy, MRI and sinus CT showed left turbinate edema, left maxillary and ethmoid sinusitis, osteolysis of the left medial orbital wall and ethmoid bony hyperplasia, with leukocytosis and neutrophilia. Preoperative differentials included invasive fungal sinusitis and lymphoma. Endoscopic sinus surgery on 15 January 2025 found mucosal swelling and purulent plaques; frozen section suggested lymphoma, but mNGS detected Prevotella and Porphyromonas and definitive histology showed chronic inflammation with lymphoid hyperplasia.

After surgery she received intravenous cefoperazone/sulbactam and methylprednisolone, with antibiotics de-escalated to imipenem/cilastatin after infectious disease consultation; C-reactive protein was 100.3 mg/L and cranial MRI and cerebrospinal fluid were unremarkable. On 25 January severe hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia developed and were treated with magnesium and potassium. Immunology showed elevated C3 and C1q and positive anti-PR3 IgG, and chest CT showed a cavitary right lower lobe nodule, leading to the diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

After electrolyte correction she received methylprednisolone pulse therapy tapered over time, intravenous cyclophosphamide 600 mg on 8 February and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis. C-reactive protein fell to 15 mg/L at discharge, methylprednisolone was tapered after discharge and a further cyclophosphamide 800 mg dose was given on 14 March. At 2-month follow-up headache had resolved and nasal congestion and rhinorrhea improved, but nasal crusting persisted.
